message.content:
**Short answer:** Yes – you can file a noise complaint in Atlanta, but it’s usually handled by the **City of Atlanta Police Department** or the **City Code Enforcement Office**, not directly by the city council. The council can help if you need to bring a broader issue to their attention, but for an individual noise problem you’ll want to use the city’s official complaint channels. --- ## How to File a Noise Complaint in Atlanta | Step | What to Do | Where/How | |------|------------|-----------| | 1 | **Gather details** | Note the time, date, location, type of noise, and any evidence (audio/video, witness statements). | | 2 | **Call 311** | Atlanta’s non-emergency hotline. 311 will route your complaint to the appropriate department.
• Phone: **(404) 656‑3111** (or dial 311 from any Atlanta cell phone). | | 3 | **Use the online portal** | Atlanta Police Department’s “Noise Complaint” form.
• Web: [https://www.atlantapd.org/311](https://www.atlantapd.org/311) (look for “Noise Complaint” or “Code Enforcement”). | | 4 | **Email or fax** | If you prefer written communication:
• Email: **noisecomplaint@atlantapd.org**
• Fax: **(404) 656‑3111** | | 5 | **Visit a City Hall office** | For in‑person filing, go to the nearest City Hall or the **Atlanta Police Department’s 311 Office**. | | 6 | **Follow up** | Keep the reference number you receive. If the issue isn’t resolved, you can contact your local city council member’s office for assistance. | --- ## Why the City Council Isn’t the First Stop - **City Council**: Sets ordinances and policies, but does not investigate individual complaints. - **Police / Code Enforcement**: Enforce the city’s noise ordinance and can issue citations or take other action. - **City Council Members**: Can help if the noise issue is part of a larger pattern (e.g., a new development, recurring nuisance). They can bring the matter to council meetings or request a city audit. --- ## Relevant Ordinance - **Atlanta Noise Ordinance** (Title 10, Chapter 10.1 of the Atlanta Municipal Code). - Sets permissible decibel limits for residential and commercial areas. - Defines “noisy” activities and penalties for violations. - Available online at the City of Atlanta’s Municipal Code portal: [https://www.atlantaga.gov/government/mayor-council/municipal-code](https://www.atlantaga.gov/government/mayor-council/municipal-code). --- ## Quick Contact List | Department | Phone | Email | Website | |------------|-------|-------|---------| | Atlanta Police Department – 311 | (404) 656‑3111 | 311@atlantapd.org | [https://www.atlantapd.org/311](https://www.atlantapd.org/311) | | City of Atlanta – Code Enforcement | (404) 656‑3111 | codeenforcement@atlantaga.gov | [https://www.atlantaga.gov/government/departments/code-enforcement](https://www.atlantaga.gov/government/departments/code-enforcement) | | City Council – Member Offices | Varies by district | Varies | [https://www.atlantaga.gov/government/mayor-council/council-members](https://www.atlantaga.gov/government/mayor-council/council-members) | --- ### Bottom line - **File the complaint with the police or code enforcement** (via 311, online form, email, or in person). - **Keep a record** of all communications and the reference number. - **If the problem persists or is part of a larger pattern**, reach out to your city council member for further assistance. Feel free to let me know if you need help locating your specific council member’s office or if you’d like a template for writing a formal complaint!
